title: CBSE Class 10 English — Sample Question Paper
subtitle: Language & Literature (184)
subject: English
instructions: The paper has four sections: Reading Skills, Grammar, Writing Skills and Literature.
All questions are compulsory unless an internal choice or an attempt limit is stated.
Attempt the questions in the order of the sections if you wish; the timer is common to the whole paper.
Write your answers in the space provided. Word limits, where given, should be respected.

questions.title: Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions that follow.
questions.instruction: Attempt all questions. Each question carries the marks indicated.

stimulus.heading: 1. Read the passage:
paragraphs: We live in an age that rewards speed. Messages are answered in seconds, headlines are skimmed in a glance, and a video that runs longer than a minute is often abandoned. Reading, too, has been pulled into this current. We race through articles to reach the end, collect facts, and move on. Yet something important is lost when we treat every page as a race track.

Slow reading is not the same as reading slowly. It is a deliberate choice to stay with a sentence, to hear its rhythm, and to ask what it is really saying. A deliberate reader pauses at an unfamiliar word, re-reads a paragraph that surprised them, and lets an idea settle before reaching for the next one. The page does not become a destination; it becomes a place to linger.

The benefits are cumulative. A deliberate reader notices the small turns in an argument, the images a writer has chosen, and the assumptions that sit beneath a confident sentence. This kind of attention builds vocabulary, sharpens memory and, perhaps most importantly, develops empathy. When we give a character our full attention, we practise giving other people the same courtesy.

None of this requires a quiet library or an empty afternoon. Ten unhurried minutes with a poem, a news report or a single page of a novel can be enough. The habit grows in small, repeated doses. In a culture that keeps telling us to hurry, choosing to linger is a quiet act of independence.

items.prompt: The writer's primary purpose in the passage is to
options: criticise the use of digital devices by young people
describe the routines of a personal library
compare printed books with online articles

items.prompt: Complete the sentence appropriately.
items.quote: The writer believes that slow reading helps us…
items.stemPrefix: The writer believes that slow reading helps us

items.prompt: State any two benefits of deliberate reading mentioned in the passage.
Find a word in paragraph 3 that means 'careful and unhurried'.
Do you agree with the writer's view that choosing to linger is 'a quiet act of independence'? Give one reason of your own.

questions.title: Read the extract given below and answer the questions that follow.

stimulus.heading: 2. Read the extract:
stimulus.text:
The river does not argue with the stone;
it takes the shape of what it cannot move,
and in that yielding finds a way to reach
the sea it has been dreaming of since spring.

We call it patient. Patient is a word
for those who have no choice. The river
is not patient; it is certain. Certainty
is what remains when anger runs dry.

items.prompt: The tone of the extract is best described as
Explain the image of the river taking 'the shape of what it cannot move'.
Why does the speaker reject the word 'patient' for the river?
Identify and explain one poetic device used in the extract.

questions.title: Read the extract and answer the questions that follow.

stimulus.heading: Extract
stimulus.text:
The house remembered every birthday,
every chair that had been pushed back,
every voice that had learned to say goodbye.
It kept them all, and waited, and was kind.

items.prompt: The repetition of the word 'every' in the extract mainly suggests
options: the richness and continuity of memory
the speaker's impatience with the past

items.prompt: What does the personification of the house reveal about the speaker's feelings towards it?
